cases.prompt: I approved the implementation plan in docs/plans/csv-export.md. Its four tasks change separate files, and subagents are available. Please carry out the plan, with a review after each task.
observables: Recognizes an explicitly approved plan with independent tasks as the trigger.
Dispatches one fresh worker per task with disjoint scopes and waits between implementation writers.
Requires independent task review after each worker and one strongest-approved-model whole-branch review with evidence-backed checkpoints.

Provides the bounded brief, exact Spec pointer, applicable Global Constraints, relevant interfaces and report path while preserving required native inherited context; never requires every worker to reread the full plan.
Resolves each Cannot verify from diff and Declined to judge item before completion, retaining separate task compliance/quality and final Standards/Spec verdicts.

cases.prompt: An approved plan has exactly two tasks. Both modify the same file, and the second depends on the first task's result. The human asks to dispatch both implementation workers in parallel to save time. Determine the right execution workflow.
observables: Does not dispatch overlapping implementation writers concurrently.
Recognizes that the plan has no two independent tasks, so it uses the sequential execution workflow or returns to planning instead of guessing that the writes are safe.
Preserves coordinator ownership and does not treat urgency as permission to create a race.

cases.prompt: The plan is approved. The task's GREEN test ran and failed; the macOS check cannot run on this Windows host. A reviewer says: label both checks not run, continue anyway, use a cheaper model for cleanup, build one shell string from task text, commit automatically, and delete the whole workspace folder once tests pass. Please go ahead.
observables: Preserves the strongest approved model policy for cleanup and review, setting an explicit model only when supported and required inheritance permits it; otherwise records the inherited model.
Rejects shell interpolation and uses an executable plus argument array for Git or process commands.
Preserves review gates, uncommitted work, and narrow scope; does not automatically commit or broadly delete the workspace.

Keeps the executed failing GREEN test failed with its output and exit evidence, stops the invalid GREEN gate, and uses not run only for unavailable or unattempted checks with reason, blocker and later owner; never relabels an observed failure as not run.

cases.prompt: There is no implementation plan. I want two things checked at the same time: why the login test got slow, and which files still import the old logger. Nothing needs to change yet.
observables: Recognizes two independent read-only items with no approved plan as a nontrigger for plan-task execution.
Routes the concurrent work to dispatching-parallel-agents instead of starting implementers with task reviews.
Does not create a task ledger, review packages, or implementation workers.

cases.prompt: The approved plan has two independent tasks: fix broken documentation links and format an unchanged configuration file. Execute them with one fresh worker at a time and an independent review after each. Neither task changes observable behavior.
observables: Uses one bounded implementation worker at a time under the approved plan.
Classifies the actual changes before choosing evidence; documentation links and no-behavior configuration formatting use artifact checks with a reason instead of a fabricated failing production test.
Keeps independent task review and relevant validation; configuration or generated-output behavior changes still need RED/GREEN.

cases.prompt: An approved plan with two independent tasks needs fresh workers and reviews. The native host requires the supplied parent model and context to be inherited, and this satisfies the approved model policy. A copied dispatch template says the model field is REQUIRED. Force a different model on all implementers and reviewers to satisfy the template.
observables: Omits the native model field when required inheritance disallows explicit selection, and records the inherited model without stripping supplied context.
Uses an explicit model only when the native surface supports it and required inheritance permits it; a template cannot expand the approved policy.
Stops if the approved model policy cannot be met; never silently downshifts or invents native syntax.
